scope: Proposition 4.2 (Fixed polygon comparison) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE Universality for Weakly Disordered FK–Ising Interfaces” (preprints/Quenched-SLE-Universality-for-Weakly-Disordered-FK-Ising-Interfaces-October-5-2026/quenched-fk-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c054f7856b32267e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exists θ0 > 0 with the following property. Fix 0 < θ < θ0, a collared orthogonal polygon P, and four distinct boundary marks in straight side interiors. Wire each of two opposite marked boundary arcs separately and leave the intervening arcs free. On the rounded lifted grid assign odds ve = √ 2 exp(θξe), where the physical-edge signs are independent and symmetric, and repeated lifted edges have the same sign. Let ϕsep δ,J and ϕsep δ,0 denote respectively this random-cluster law and the pure law on the same graph and with the same boundary partition. If Aδ is the event of an actual open path between the two wired arcs, then ϕsep δ,J (Aδ) − ϕsep δ,0 (Aδ) −→ 0 in environmental probability as δ ↓ 0. (4.1) The disorder threshold is independent of the fixed polygon and marks. The conclusion also holds on the dual square grid.
